title: Storage Capacity in PACS
body_text:
Under the Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector 12  PACS/Cooperative Societies with a capacity of 0.52 LMT have been identified in 12 districts of the state and detailed project report in respect of all 13 projects have been prepared . However, construction is yet to be started by the States. Further, one godown of 1,500 MT capacity has already been constructed in Kotwa Pandey PACS in Mirzapur district of Uttar Pradesh. The Plan is demand-driven and implementation is undertaken in phased manner on the proposals received from State /UTs and therefore no state wise target is fixed. However, as per the AMI guidelines of DA&FW, construction of godowns by PACS/Cooperative Societies to be completed within 18 months and to submit completion documents for final subsidy claims. However, an extension of up to 6 additional months can be allowed if the reasons for delay are fully justified.
Under the Plan, financial assistance is available only for construction of new scientific storage infrastructure at PACS/other cooperative society level. All the godowns under decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector are created after the launch of the plan. Old or dilapidated PACS buildings are not treated as modern scientific warehouses under the plan.
To enable faster sanction of loan, a series of measures were undertaken under the plan. Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), the loan repayment period has been enhanced from 2+5 years to 2+8 years, thereby providing greater flexibility to borrowers.  Nabhsanrakshan scheme credit guarantee was also extended to PACS at par with Farmer Producer Organization (FPO). Under the Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) Scheme, the capital subsidy has been enhanced from 25% to 33.33%, the margin money requirement has been reduced from 20% to 10%. Besides this the Plan also utilizes NABARD's special refinance scheme to significantly reduce the financial burden on participating cooperatives. When combined with the 3% interest subvention available under the AIF, the effective loan interest rate for PACS is reduced to 1% under Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector.
Further, under decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector eligible cooperative societies, including PACS, may establish infrastructure on either self-owned land or leased land. Land allocation is facilitated by the concerned State Governments, wherever required. Issues relating to land availability, loan sanction and financial capacity of PACS/other cooperative societies are addressed in coordination with the State Governments and the implementing agencies.
There is no such provision for separate quota or special subsidy for storage charges under the decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector.
This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.
*****
AK/AP

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Ministry of Cooperation informed that under the Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector, 12 PACS/Cooperative Societies with a combined capacity of 0.52 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) have been identified across 12 districts, with detailed project reports prepared for all 13 projects, though construction is yet to begin. One godown of 1,500 MT capacity has already been completed at Kotwa Pandey PACS in Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh. The reply also detailed financial incentives introduced to speed up implementation, including an extended AIF loan repayment period, extension of the Nabhsanrakshan credit guarantee to PACS, higher AMI capital subsidy, reduced margin money, and an effective loan interest rate of 1% for PACS.
enrichment.context:
The Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector, part of the broader initiative to establish the 'world's largest grain storage plan in the cooperative sector', was launched to strengthen agricultural marketing infrastructure by building scientific storage (godowns) at the level of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and other cooperative societies. It aims to reduce post-harvest losses, curb distress selling by farmers, decongest central/state warehousing agencies like FCI and state civil supplies corporations, and enable PACS to diversify into activities like storage, custom hiring, and retail besides their traditional credit function. The plan is being implemented by leveraging multiple existing schemes—the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), the Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) sub-scheme under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, and NABARD's refinance mechanisms—rather than being a standalone budgetary scheme, reflecting the government's broader strategy of convergence across ministries for rural infrastructure creation.

This initiative is part of the Ministry of Cooperation's larger mandate since its creation in 2021 to revitalize the cooperative sector, with PACS (over 1 lakh in number) envisioned as multi-service centres under the 'Sahakar se Samriddhi' vision. The financial sweeteners mentioned—enhanced AIF repayment tenure, extended Nabhsanrakshan credit guarantee (earlier limited to FPOs), higher AMI subsidy, and reduced margin money—are aimed at overcoming PACS' traditionally weak financial capacity to access institutional credit, a persistent bottleneck in rural cooperative infrastructure development.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector', mentioned frequently in news, primarily aims to create storage infrastructure at the level of which of the following?
options: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and other cooperative societies
prelims_questions.explanation: The Plan is implemented to build scientific storage (godowns) infrastructure at the level of PACS and other cooperative societies, as described in the release.

prelims_questions.question: Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)-linked benefits for PACS under the Decentralized Grain Storage Plan, which of the following changes has been made to support cooperative societies?
options: Margin money requirement increased from 10% to 20%
Loan repayment period reduced from 2+8 years to 2+5 years
Capital subsidy under AMI enhanced from 25% to 33.33%
Interest subvention withdrawn entirely for PACS
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the AMI capital subsidy has been enhanced from 25% to 33.33% while margin money was reduced from 20% to 10% and the AIF repayment period was extended from 2+5 to 2+8 years.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector for strengthening Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and addressing India's post-harvest storage gap. What challenges hinder its implementation at the state level?

Examine the role of convergence between the Ministry of Cooperation, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, and NABARD in financing rural infrastructure schemes such as the Decentralized Grain Storage Plan. How does such convergence affect scheme implementation and accountability?
